segments.he: ר' ישראל מקארדן ז"ל שנתקרב לחסידות רבינו ז"ל למד ושימש את ר' משה ברסלבר ז"ל ולמד ר' משה ז"ל עמו בספרי רבינו ז"ל מהצדיק האמת שיכול לעשות כ"ד מיני פדיונות ושאר ענינים מדריגות של הצדיק האמת ענה ואמר ר' ישראל שגם המפורסם שלו אוחז במדריגות אלו (כי' הוא הי' מקירה שהאמין מאד במפורסמים שבזמננו) ענה ר' משה ז"ל ואמר לו "אתה שקר ומפורסמך שקר דאס ביזס א שקר אין דיין רבי איז א שקר" ולא רצה עוד לדבר אתו ועבר עוד איזה זמן ועבד בעבודת ה' והבין האמת אז פייס את ר' משה הנ"ל ולמד אצלו אח"כ ונתקרב על ידו לחסידות רבינו ז"ל.
segments.en:
The story of Chacham Yechezkel — a great Sephardic sage, a holy man of G-d, a Kohen, a great Tzaddik with a revelation of Eliyahu HaNavi. The Sephardic sages of Tzfas relate much about him. What I remember I will write here:

He was for thirty years closed and sealed at Meron, at the grave of the divine Tanna Reb Shimon bar Yochai. At that time there was still no Moshav Zekenim [home for elders] there, and in the courtyard of the holy grave not a single person lived — only he was there always alone. His son Chacham Tziyon Kohen of Tzfas would send him food and all his needs through a driver [a man who had donkeys and would travel once or twice a week to bring him provisions]. He sat there studying Torah and serving G-d day and night, always keeping watch over the lamp. He would go to the Magido — the spring of Meron — where there is a place called the mikveh of Rabbi Shimon. He would go there at midnight and before midnight. And the place is wilderness with wild animals — wolves and leopards — even today, and certainly then when there was no settlement at all. Once he left the courtyard open and when he returned to the synagogue of Rashbi where he always sat, he found it open and full of wolves and wild animals. He took his staff and drove them outside. From then on he endeavored to build a mikveh in the courtyard — and that is the mikveh that is now in the courtyard: he built it.

Once he commanded the sages who came to the grave of Rashbi that they should lower him into the cave where Rashbi lies [for the Ari would be lowered into the cave, as the entrance of the cave was then open]. When they had lowered him halfway, his face became very pale and he cried out that they should pull him back outside. Another time, Chacham Yechezkel suddenly went blind in both eyes [because there is danger in being there alone by the grave of Rashbi, as is written in the writings of the Ari]. When on Friday afternoon the driver came to bring his Shabbos provisions, he found him completely blind — not even able to perceive light — only feeling his way around. He warned the driver to tell no one about this — not his son, not anyone. The driver, when he returned to Tzfas on Friday afternoon, was asked by the son about his father's welfare — and the driver answered evasively. The son understood something was amiss, pressed him, made him swear, and heard the story. The son took the driver the next week to Meron. When they arrived, Chacham Yechezkel saw them coming and looked at the driver with an angry face — but the son immediately spoke up and said: "The driver is not at fault — I made him swear." And Chacham Yechezkel told his son the full story: immediately after he had asked the driver to lead him to the holy grave, the driver led him there as described, and he placed his head on the holy grave and begged greatly with weeping: "I give up my soul to be here with you and serve Hashem — and why does this happen to me? And what will the world say? This will be a chillul Hashem!" And he pleaded this way until he fell asleep on the holy grave. And he dreamed that he saw Rashbi, who said to him: "Do not be afraid — you will have a complete healing soon." When he woke, he saw that he was completely healed and well like any person.

Before his passing, there was an event: the lamp by which he studied went out. He kept going back to it to see if it was burning — and saw that it had gone out again — and he kept relighting it. He sensed there was a great serpent there, and the serpent fled to the other room — the room that today is where the men stand at the holy grave. He went after it, and when he came to the inner room by the holy grave, he saw Reb Shimon bar Yochai sitting there. And Rashbi said to him: "Know that the time has come for you to depart from the world. Your place is in Tzfas. And because you were always here with me in Torah and the service of G-d, you have the merit that I appeared to you before your passing. In three more days you will be taken from the world — therefore travel to Tzfas and give instructions to your household." And so it was: on that day the driver came, and Chacham Yechezkel traveled with him to Tzfas, gave his instructions to his household — and was taken from the world in peace. And there is a beautiful story about Chacham Yechezkel who went with other Kohanim to the burial cave of Aharon HaKohen — but I do not remember it well enough to record it properly.
